problem:
Consider the function $f(x,y)=(1-x)(y+2)^{2}.$ What are the missing entries in the following sign table of $f(x,y)?$

| $y>-2$ |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $y<-2$ |  |  |
|  | $x<1$ | $x>1$ |

feedback.problem:
Consider the function $f(x,y)=-y(x-2).$ What are the missing entries in the following sign table of $f(x,y)?$

| $y>0$ |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $y<0$ |  |  |
|  | $x<2$ | $x>2$ |
feedback.worked_solution:
Notice that $f(x,y)$ equals zero when $x=2$ and $y=0.$ These lines divide the $xy$-plane into four regions, as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14041262/assets/41e876c3444c2fc9a5103c16b9c6c3b34a4c7596082e4c8235a5e86cd57f8570.png)

To determine the sign of $f(x,y)$ in each region, we pick four test points, one for each region.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14041262/assets/c21e4edde44891c4173420575268750fc0f1f407ba8503953de86a9cc72297dc.png)

Next, we calculate the sign of $f(x,y)$ in each region using a sign table:

|  | Test point | $-y$ | $(x-2)$ | $f(x,y)$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Top-Left | $(1,1)$ | $-$ | $-$ | $+$ |
| Top-Right | $(3,1)$ | $-$ | $+$ | $-$ |
| Bottom-Left | $(1,-1)$ | $+$ | $-$ | $-$ |
| Bottom-Right | $(3,-1)$ | $+$ | $+$ | $+$ |

 

Using the *last* column of the table above, we get the following picture:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14041262/assets/b668aa9647600567c5d6deccbe3830a26561c06f920e2db2364e632f26c39eff.png)

Finally, we fill in the required sign table.

| $y>0$ | $+$ | $-$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $y<0$ | $-$ | $+$ |
|  | $x<2$ | $x>2$ |
